strengths: Addresses a relevant practical problem: integrating multiple MLLMs without additional training, with genuine benefits for extensibility and modularity
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 10+ diverse benchmarks spanning general understanding, vision, temporal reasoning, and specialized domains
Thoughtful system design with three well-motivated components addressing distinct challenges (task routing, memory management, latency optimization)
Strong empirical results on multiple benchmarks (88.54% on MMBench-EN, 70.04% on MMMU, notable improvements on video understanding)
Clear presentation with effective figures illustrating the framework and concrete workflow examples
Practical system that demonstrates feasibility of achieving multimodal capabilities through intelligent orchestration rather than end-to-end training
weaknesses: CRITICAL: Unfair experimental comparisons - the system uses multiple large models (7+ expert models) as executors while comparing against single models (GPT-4o, VITA). The paper acknowledges 60% of calls to 32B model but does not properly address this fundamental unfairness. Fair comparisons require joint training baselines or equal computational budget comparisons.

Insufficient computational cost analysis - claims 10.3% latency reduction but only measures TTS time (0.204→0.183s), not total system latency, FLOPs, or memory requirements. Efficiency claims are not substantiated given the use of multiple large models running in sequence with orchestration overhead.

No ablation studies provided - impossible to assess individual component contributions (controller, memory, parallel TTS). Cannot determine whether improvements come from routing, memory pooling, or task-specific expert selection. The 7.8% video improvement is attributed broadly without mechanistic analysis.

Limited technical novelty - controller routing uses straightforward prompt engineering with special tokens (not novel), memory system uses standard JSON storage (used in existing agents), parallel batch TTS is engineering optimization. Contribution is primarily system-level integration rather than methodological advances.

Reproducibility concerns - many baseline results 'referenced from official papers' rather than reproduced under identical conditions; critical implementation details under-specified (control token definition, token generation mechanism, runtime prompt construction, fallback behaviors); no code release mentioned

Misleading 'training-free' framing - all components (controller LLM and expert models) are pre-trained; only composition lacks training. More accurately 'composition without additional training,' not 'training-free,' overselling the novelty

Missing failure mode analysis - no investigation of when orchestration fails, error rates in control token generation, or performance degradation under model selection errors. Sensitivity to incorrect routing decisions not addressed.

Vague critical design specifications - memory compression strategy left unspecified (rule-based vs auxiliary LLM), runtime prompt construction inadequately detailed, semantic classification for modality selection lacks implementation details, TTS segmentation rules are basic heuristics without comparison to alternatives

Insufficient ablation and sensitivity analysis - no study showing impact of removing orchestration reasoning vs simple routing, no prompt sensitivity analysis, no investigation of controller LLM size effects, no comparison of different expert model combinations

Limited analysis of complex multimodal reasoning - example workflow (garden flowers) is simple; no analysis of challenging multi-step tasks requiring true cross-modal understanding; specialized task performance highly variable (MathVision 39.11% vs CC-OCR 79.11%) without explanation
